_: The Abyss, level 1, at life scale.
metresPerUnit is measured, not chosen. Underworld's GLBs are in TILES
(levgeo.HeightScale = 0.25, one tile = 1.0). The door leaf is 208 model
door is 0.8125 tiles and a 2 m door makes a tile 2.4615 m.
It cross-checks against the room the door stands in: the level-wide ceiling
is Ceiling 16 x HeightScale 0.25 = 4.0 tiles, and the start-room floor is at
3.0 (the exported camera sits at 3.55, floor plus a 0.55 eye height). One
tile of head-room over a 0.8125-tile door: 2.46 m of ceiling over a 2 m
door, which is what a dungeon corridor should be.
spawn.pos is the FLOOR, not the eye — the eye height comes from the
headset, which knows it better than we do.
_fog: The reach. 11 m in a 2.46 m corridor is about three rooms ahead.
_torch: Brightness, not reach. Modulating the fog alone animates how far you can
see and never makes anything brighter, which is why the first version read
as the room breathing rather than as a flame. radial:true puts the flicker
on a fragment patch that can actually dim a wall; the fog keeps 30% of the
modulation so the reach still wavers (xrflame.js REACH_SHARE).
The signal is 1/f — five octaves, 0.7 to 19.6 Hz, amplitude falling with
frequency — because that is what flame luminance measures as. Plus a fast
attack and slow release (fire flares quicker than it fades) and a slow gust
channel. Dimmer is redder: warm at full, cool at the bottom.
